p: If you're down on holiday and the forecast has turned, a session here slots in nicely around the rest of the day without wrecking your plans. Racing itself is short and sharp, so you can book a slot, race, and still have plenty of the day left for the town.

Pair it with other indoor options and you've got a proper wet-weather itinerary. The Oceanarium sits right by the pier, and the Russell-Cotes Art Gallery and Museum, a grand Victorian villa perched on the East Cliff, is one of the town's real hidden gems.
If the sun breaks through later, head for Boscombe Pier or take the walk out to Hengistbury Head, where the views over Christchurch Harbour are cracking on a clear evening.

Getting around is simple too. Bournemouth's town centre is compact, and buses run regularly along the coast between Bournemouth, Boscombe and Poole, so you won't need to move the car once it's parked. That leaves more time for ice cream on the front once the racing's done.

Booking ahead is a good idea in the school holidays, when half the families in town have the same idea as you. And if you've got younger ones with you, check the junior rules before you promise anyone a race.
